beginning_sequence.title: You just did the hard part
beginning_sequence.body:
Most people who struggle with this never tell anyone, never measure it, and never make a plan. You just did all three in one sitting.

That wasn't a small thing. Deciding to face this — with a method instead of another midnight promise — is the step that everything else builds on.

So before Day 1: a two-minute tour of what you've actually signed up for.

beginning_sequence.title: How this works
beginning_sequence.body:
This is a 6-week program built on four approaches from published clinical research: CBT (map and re-engineer your pattern), mindfulness (outlast urges instead of obeying them), ACT (put your energy into your values, not the tug-of-war), and motivational science (keep your own reasons in the driver's seat).

The shape: about ten minutes a day — one short lesson, one exercise, one evening check-in. Each week builds on the last. Nothing here is filler; every day exists because research or clinical practice put it there.

beginning_sequence.title: The honest expectations
beginning_sequence.body:
Some days will feel easy. Some won't — that's not the program failing; difficulty is part of the design, the way sore muscles are part of training.

Urges will still come, especially early. You'll learn to ride them. If a slip ever happens, there's a protocol for that too — a debrief, not a shame spiral. Nothing you build here can be un-built by one bad night.

Your progress has a scoreboard: the screening score you just took. You'll re-measure every two weeks and watch the trend — that number, not perfection, is what winning looks like.

beginning_sequence.title: Your six weeks
beginning_sequence.body: Here's the whole road. You only ever need to walk today's ten minutes of it.

week_2.title: Week 2 — Know Your Pattern
week_2.body:
Last week you decided and committed. This week you become an expert on your own loop: when it starts, what feeds it, and the chain it runs on.

Expect detective work — mapping your triggers, reconstructing real episodes, and re-engineering your environment so fewer battles ever start. By Sunday you'll hold something most people never have: a written map of exactly how this happens to you, and where it's weakest.

week_3.title: Week 3 — Ride the Urge
week_3.body:
You know the pattern. Now you learn what to do when an urge is actually here.

This is the most skills-heavy week: urge surfing, defusing the mind's sales pitches, dropping the tug-of-war rope. You'll practice while calm — the way anything worth trusting under pressure gets practiced. By the end, you'll have written your own urge script: exact instructions from your calmest self to your hardest moment.

week_4.title: Week 4 — Live Your Values
week_4.body:
The first three weeks were about the problem. From here on, it's about the life.

This week you choose the two values worth organizing this season around, turn them into small daily actions, and learn the program's biggest reframe: your urges have been pointing at what you actually need all along. Expect this week to feel different — less about resisting something, more about building someone.

week_5.title: Week 5 — Rebuild the Life
week_5.body:
Skills protect you in the moment. Infrastructure protects you all day.

This week you audit and reinforce the five pillars everything stands on — sleep, movement, connection, purpose, play — and plant defenses directly into your risk windows. It's the most practical week of the program: by Sunday, your calendar itself will be working for you.

week_6.title: Week 6 — Stay Free
week_6.body:
The final week is about permanence.

You'll forecast the storms of the next 90 days, build your early-warning system, assemble your complete relapse-prevention plan, and compress six weeks of work into one Emergency Card for your hardest minute. Then: your maintenance rhythm, and graduation. Finish strong — this week's work is what you keep forever.

welcome_back: Good to see you. The program waited — no catching up needed, today's session is right here.
Welcome back. Life happens; the road doesn't move. Pick up exactly where you left off.
You came back — that's the whole skill. Today's ten minutes are ready when you are.
